task.description:
Update Letflow's protocol docs so agents actually use the new letflow-queue capabilities. The service change is already merged and deployed and its behaviour is VERIFIED LIVE (see context.upstream_change) -- you are documenting what the service now does, not proposing anything.

WHAT CHANGED IN THE SERVICE, and why:

  1. **`register_task` now allocates the issue id.** Every response carries a new `issue_ref` field: for `task_type: "issue"` it is `"ISS-"` plus the zero-padded task id (task 187 -> `"ISS-0187"`); `null` for requirements. For issue-type tasks the service ALSO rewrites the task title to carry that ref as a prefix, stripping and replacing any `ISS-NNNN:` the caller supplied. Only a LEADING token is replaced -- an `ISS-` reference elsewhere in a title is a genuine cross-reference and survives verbatim.

     This exists because the current numbering rule in ISSUE_QUEUE.md -- 'check the highest existing NNNN under docs/issues/, increment' -- is a read-then-write race with no lock between the halves, and it has now collided EIGHT times across concurrent sessions. The eighth is the decisive one: that run scanned `docs/issues/` across every REMOTE BRANCH before choosing, which is exactly what docs/anti-patterns.md prescribes as the mitigation, and it collided anyway, because the colliding numbers did not exist on any branch at the moment it looked. A scan cannot reserve a number; only an allocator can. The queue's `id` is an autoincrement primary key, so it is allocated atomically and no two hosts can ever receive the same one.

  2. **`register_task` accepts an optional `github_issue_number`** and, when given, adopts it instead of creating a second GitHub issue. A number already linked to another task is rejected (unique index) rather than re-pointed.

THREE FILES TO UPDATE.

**A. docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md -- the numbering rule, which is the substantive change.** Its Procedure step 1 currently says to assign the next available local id by scanning docs/issues/ and incrementing. That instruction must go. The new order is: ORCH calls `register_task` FIRST, and the returned `issue_ref` IS the id -- the local record is then written to `docs/issues/<issue_ref>.yaml`.

  **This inverts an existing instruction, so reconcile it explicitly rather than leaving two rules standing.** docs/anti-patterns.md currently says 'File the local record before opening the GitHub issue, and put the id in the GH title', whose stated reason was that a GitHub issue citing a local file that has since been overwritten is the worst end state. Under the new order the GitHub issue is created first (by the service, as part of `register_task`) and the local file is written immediately after, within the same agent turn. Explain why that is now the safer order: the id can no longer be wrong, the overwrite hazard the old advice guarded against was itself a CONSEQUENCE of guessed numbering, and the id now appears in the GH title automatically rather than depending on an agent remembering to put it there. Do not silently drop the old advice -- state that it is superseded and why.

  Also cover: `queue_task_id` and the issue id are now the same integer (`ISS-0187` <-> task 187), which makes a later WF-03 run's `set_lock` target derivable from the filename; and the 2a instruction not to call `gh issue create` separately still stands, with the `github_issue_number` adoption path documented as the escape hatch for an issue that genuinely was filed first (e.g. by a human).

**B. docs/agents/protocols/TASK_QUEUE.md -- the `register_task` section.** Document the `issue_ref` response field and the optional `github_issue_number` request field, and update the 'Record it back into the source record' bullet: for `task_type: "issue"` the record's FILENAME now comes from `issue_ref`, and `queue_task_id` is the same number. Keep the existing warning about never inventing a placeholder `impl_order` -- it is still correct and now has a second reason (a guessed id is also a guessed filename).

**C. docs/anti-patterns.md -- the ISS-collision entry.** Its final section currently says the structural fix is deferred: 'Until ISSUE_QUEUE.md gains a real reservation mechanism (the obvious candidate: derive the id from register_task's returned impl_order...)' and instructs agents to scan remote branches and expect collisions as routine. That is now out of date and, worse, actively harmful if followed, since it tells agents to keep guessing. APPEND an update recording that the predicted fix has landed and is deployed, that the mechanism is exactly the one that entry proposed, and that the scan-and-renumber routine it prescribes is superseded for NEW issues. Keep the historical account intact -- append, never rewrite. Note that the eighth occurrence is what motivated the fix, and that it is the strongest evidence in the entry precisely because the run followed the prescribed mitigation and collided anyway.

ONE FACT TO RECORD SOMEWHERE SENSIBLE (your judgement which file): issue ids will now JUMP from the hand-numbered range (highest existing is ISS-0119) to the queue-allocated range (currently ISS-0186 and upward), and will be NON-CONTIGUOUS thereafter because ids are shared with requirement-type tasks. That is expected, not missing records. A future reader finding no ISS-0120..0185 should not go looking for lost files.

Do NOT change any code, and do not touch docs/issues/*.yaml. Do NOT retro-renumber any existing issue record -- the existing hand-numbered ones keep their numbers.
acceptance_criteria: AC1 -- ISSUE_QUEUE.md's Procedure no longer instructs anyone to derive an issue id by scanning docs/issues/ and incrementing. The register_task-first order is stated concretely enough to follow without inference, including that the local record's filename comes from the returned issue_ref

AC2 -- The inversion of the 'local record before GitHub issue' advice is addressed explicitly, with the old advice named as superseded and the reason the new order is safe stated -- not silently dropped and not left contradicting the anti-patterns entry
AC3 -- ISSUE_QUEUE.md documents the github_issue_number adoption path, and that step 2a's 'do not also call gh issue create' still stands

AC4 -- TASK_QUEUE.md's register_task section documents the issue_ref response field and the optional github_issue_number request field, and its record-it-back bullet reflects that an issue's filename now derives from issue_ref with queue_task_id being the same integer
AC5 -- TASK_QUEUE.md's existing warning against inventing a placeholder impl_order is preserved, not removed

AC6 -- docs/anti-patterns.md's ISS-collision entry carries an APPENDED update: the deferred structural fix has landed and is deployed, it is the mechanism that entry itself proposed, and the scan-and-renumber routine is superseded for new issues. The historical account above it is unchanged -- verify with git diff that your change to that entry is purely additive
AC7 -- The id discontinuity (no ISS-0120..0185) is recorded somewhere a future reader will find it, framed as expected rather than as missing records

AC8 -- Every factual claim about the service's behaviour matches context.upstream_change. Do not describe behaviour that was not verified there; if you believe something else is true, flag it rather than asserting it
AC9 -- No file outside the three named docs and your own handoff is modified. No code, no docs/issues/*.yaml, no renumbering of existing records

result.summary: All three protocol docs updated to the register_task-allocated issue id. ISSUE_QUEUE.md: Procedure step 1's 'scan docs/issues/ and increment' instruction is removed outright and replaced with 'the id comes back from register_task as issue_ref; until step 2a returns, refer to the finding by title'; step 2a documents issue_ref (ISS- + zero-padded task id, null for requirements), the leading-token-only title rewrite, the github_issue_number adoption path and its already-taken rejection, and restates that 'do NOT also call gh issue create separately' still stands; step 2b's queue-unreachable branch no longer implies a local number (report the finding to ORCH for registration; any interim GH issue is later adopted via github_issue_number); step 3/4 take the filename from issue_ref. A new 'Where the id comes from (2026-08-21)' section names the anti-patterns 'local record before GitHub issue' advice as superseded and gives three reasons the inverted order is safe (the overwrite hazard was a consequence of guessed numbering, not ordering; the id can no longer be wrong; the id reaches the GH title by construction rather than by diligence), states queue_task_id == the issue id so a WF-03 set_lock target is derivable from the filename, and records the ISS-0120..0185 discontinuity as expected. TASK_QUEUE.md: register_task section documents the optional github_issue_number request field and the issue_ref response field, the record-it-back bullet now derives an issue's filename from issue_ref with queue_task_id the same integer, and the placeholder-impl_order warning is preserved verbatim with an appended second reason (a guessed id is also a guessed filename). anti-patterns.md: a purely additive UPDATE 2026-08-21 appended to the ISS-collision entry (git diff --numstat: 61 insertions, 0 deletions on that file) recording that the deferred structural fix landed, is deployed and is exactly the mechanism the entry itself proposed, that the scan-and-renumber routine is superseded for new issues while the handling of existing hand-numbered records is not, and that the eighth occurrence (WF03-ISS0106-20260821, records renumbered to ISS-0118/ISS-0119) is the decisive evidence because it followed the prescribed remote-branch scan and collided anyway. Every service-behaviour claim is traceable to context.upstream_change; nothing beyond it is asserted. No code, no docs/issues/*.yaml, no renumbering.

issues.description: ISSUE_QUEUE.md step 2b (letflow-queue unreachable) previously told the agent to file under a locally-derived ISS-NNNN. With local derivation removed there is no allocator in that path, so the step now says to report the finding to ORCH for registration once the queue is reachable (with an interim gh issue adopted later via github_issue_number) rather than to invent a number. That is a procedural choice made here, not a service behaviour verified in context.upstream_change -- flagging it so ORCH can confirm or amend it rather than have it stand unreviewed.

The eighth collision was not previously recorded in docs/anti-patterns.md (its entry stops at the seventh, ISS-0107). Its account here was re-derived from the repo -- docs/issues/ISS-0118.yaml and ISS-0119.yaml's renumbered_from/renumbered_note fields, filed by WF03-ISS0106-20260821 against PR #371's concurrently-allocated ISS-0110..0117 -- not taken from the handoff alone.

No docs/status/requirement_status.yaml event was appended: this ad-hoc run carries no requirement (context.requirement_ids is empty) and nothing in docs/requirements.yaml was flipped, so there is no requirement status to record. Noting it explicitly so its absence reads as deliberate rather than as a skipped DOC-UPDATER step.
